scope: Original code executed on each required route of the frozen slice, attributed to function and code image, against the functions the shared reconstruction library names. Addresses, counts and hashes only.

method.capture: One cold-boot capture per route in the observation-trace shell with the coverage extension (tools/reference/instruction_trace.py CoverageTrace, nix/reference-trace.h): per 600-frame window, every executed RAM word with its first and last fetched instruction word, and SHA-256 of the declared code ranges at the window start and end. Each capture reproduces the final RAM of an earlier capture of the same route; eleven match an uninstrumented core exactly.
method.attribution: An executed word belongs to an image when its fetched instruction equals the image word at that address and the image code range is loaded at the window start or end; otherwise a run of at least four contiguous executed words matching one image identifies it. Words equal in two loaded images are counted in both and reported as ambiguous. Functions are Ghidra function bodies.
method.function_boundaries: The listed private Ghidra surveys. p1cov-supplement-v1 re-ran the same PrepareSliceOverlay/ExportSliceSurvey recipe with entry candidates from executed code outside every surveyed function (jal targets and starts after jr ra); only functions that overlap no base-survey body are added. Words still outside every function are listed per route.
method.reconstruction_set: Addresses in comments of src/reconstruction and include/xem/reconstruction that are known function entries. Automatic: the address leads the comment directly above a C++ definition or declaration. Every other executed mention was reviewed by hand; passing mentions (callers, gates, presentation callbacks, layout notes, service stubs that throw) are excluded. An address that is an entry in several images keeps the image of its source subsystem.
method.partial: reconstructed_partial: a throw in the C++ definition that stops on an unreconstructed path (MissingDependency, Unrecovered*/Unsupported*, or a message saying not recovered/reconstructed) names an original address that the route executes, other than the function entry itself; or the source comment states that only part of the original is reconstructed. An executed throw address is necessary, not sufficient, for the throw to fire. Throws without a literal address, and differences in executed basic blocks, are not determined.
method.setup: The guarded Kernel MENU setup window (frames before field request or title) is excluded from the counts.
